newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says overjoyed by Israel copter crash.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says overjoyed by Israel copter crash.

text.p: Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah said on Wednesday the mid-air crash of two Lebanon-bound Israeli military helicopters that killed 73 soldiers was an act of God.

"We consider what happened a success granted by God...I will use this occassion to express big happiness and ask our people and loved ones to pray to God and thank him," Hizbollah deputy chief Sheikh Na'eem Qassem told reporters of the Tuesday crash.

"What happened was a Godly revenge for the children of Qana and for all those suffering and all those killed in Lebanon," the bearded cleric said, referring to the killing of some 100 civilians when Israeli gunners shelled the south Lebanon village of Qana during a 17-day blitz against Hizbollah last April.

Some 200 people, main civilians, were killed in the April blitz dubbed by Israel "Operation Grapes of Wrath". The relentless air, land and sea bombardment of south Lebanon caused extensive damage but failed to crush Hizbollah.
Hizbollah (Party of God), financed and armed by Iran, is fighting to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 allied local militia from a border zone they occupy in south Lebanon.
The 73 Israeli soldiers killed in the crash exceeded by three the number of fatalities inflicted by Hizbollah against Israeli soldiers in south Lebanon in the past three years.

The two U.S.-made Sikorsky CH-53 transporters collided and crashed in northern Israel near the Lebanese border on Tuesday night. They were on their way to the 15-km (nine-mile)-wide occupation zone which Israel carved out in 1985 to repel guerrilla attacks.
